nodes.label: Fake Directory Listing Honeypot

nodes.label: AI Deception Prompt Template
nodes.rationale: Only {path} and {query_part} substituted; other braces raise KeyError. Prompt pushes 'deployed not designed' realism.

nodes.label: Ignored IPs
nodes.rationale: Never tracked/banned/exported and purged at startup; defaults cover loopback, RFC1918, link-local, CGNAT.

nodes.label: IPv6 Ignore
nodes.rationale: Rotating IPv6 proxy pools burn a fresh address per request, making per-address tracking worthless.

nodes.label: Scheduled Task Batch Sizes
nodes.rationale: Defaults sized for a 256Mi pod; raw HTTP bodies are multi-KB so bigger batches cost memory.

nodes.label: AI-Generated Deception Pages
nodes.rationale: OpenRouter/OpenAI generated pages, cached, daily rate limited, graceful fallback.

nodes.label: Banlist Federation
nodes.rationale: Instances publish banlists on an unauthenticated path and merge upstream lists into local ban decisions.

nodes.label: Deployment Modes (Standalone vs Scalable)
nodes.rationale: Standalone: SQLite WAL + in-memory dict, single instance; Scalable: PostgreSQL + Redis multi-tier TTL cache, horizontal scaling.

nodes.label: IP Reputation Scoring
nodes.rationale: Weighted scoring over risky methods, robots.txt violations, timing anomalies, UA consistency, attack URLs -> attacker/bad_crawler/good_crawler/regular_user/unknown.

nodes.label: Krawl Dashboard
nodes.rationale: Served on a random or configured secret path to stay hidden from scanners; password protects sensitive tabs.

nodes.label: TLSH Threat-Intel Capture / Campaign Clustering
nodes.rationale: Hash-payloads task fuzzy-hashes captured payloads once with a payload_hash_watermark backward sweep, clustering near-duplicates into campaigns.

nodes.label: Docker Build and Push Workflow
nodes.rationale: Multi-arch (amd64/arm64) image tagged from helm/Chart.yaml appVersion; main gets :latest, other branches get version-branch suffix; registry build cache.

nodes.label: Helm Package and Push Workflow
nodes.rationale: Rewrites Chart.yaml version/appVersion with branch suffix to keep chart and image produced by docker-build-push on the same tag.

nodes.label: Helm Chart Validation Job
nodes.rationale: Lints and templates chart, then asserts rendered image tag matches Chart appVersion and release-revision annotation.

nodes.label: PR Lint & Dependency Checks Job
nodes.rationale: Auto-fixes with ruff/black and pushes back only on same-repo PRs; fork PRs skip to avoid false passes since GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only. [skip ci] avoids re-trigger.

nodes.label: Security Scan Job (Bandit + pip-audit)
nodes.rationale: Fails PR only on HIGH severity Bandit findings; pip-audit is advisory.

nodes.label: Weekly Banlist Update Workflow
nodes.rationale: Every Saturday fetches attacker IPs from demo instance export-ips API and opens a PR updating banlist.txt.

nodes.label: Scalable Dev Compose Stack
nodes.rationale: Builds from local source with compose watch rebuild; -dev suffixed names to coexist with other stacks.

nodes.label: Fail2Ban Integration
nodes.rationale: bantime 30 days matches 30-day file rotation; permanent bans discouraged since attacker IPs rotate.

nodes.label: Krawl Web Honeypot
nodes.rationale: Cloud-native deception server that wastes attacker resources to distinguish malicious behavior from legitimate crawlers.

nodes.label: Marker-based PR Comment Upsert
nodes.rationale: Bot finds an existing comment by HTML marker and updates it instead of spamming new comments.

nodes.label: Env Var over config.yaml Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: KRAWL_ + upper-cased setting path overrides config.yaml; suited to Docker deployments.

nodes.label: Self-hosted Debian Runner venv Setup
nodes.rationale: actions/setup-python cannot fetch Python for this distro; uses system python3 in a venv to avoid PEP 668 issues.

nodes.label: robots.txt Trap Paths
nodes.rationale: Disallow entries advertise bait paths; crawlers ignoring robots.txt hit them and are flagged; also excluded from generative AI page creation.

nodes.label: TasksMaster (APScheduler task orchestrator)
nodes.rationale: Tasks auto-discovered from src/tasks; each sweeping task takes a bounded slice per run.

nodes.label: Data Retention Job
nodes.rationale: Preserves credentials, suspicious logs and IPs with suspicious history; removes only non-suspicious/stale data.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL pg_dump Backup
nodes.rationale: --no-owner --no-privileges for portability; 5-minute timeout prevents hung backups.

nodes.label: Scalable Mode (PostgreSQL + Redis)
nodes.rationale: Horizontal scaling with shared DB, RollingUpdate strategy.

nodes.label: SQLite to PostgreSQL Migration Script
nodes.rationale: Krawl must be stopped and data backed up; batch insert with row-by-row fallback and verification summary.

nodes.label: Standalone Mode (SQLite + in-memory cache)
nodes.rationale: Simplest setup with no external deps; K8s Recreate strategy due to SQLite file lock.

nodes.label: SQLite Atomic Backup (sqlite3.backup + rename)
nodes.rationale: Writes temp file then atomically renames so partial backup never replaces a good one; safe under WAL.

nodes.label: Redis Cache Tiers (hot-path, table, warmup)
nodes.rationale: Hot-path tier avoids a PostgreSQL round-trip per request; table tier shared across replicas; warmup tier refreshed by background task.

nodes.label: Single-Pod Task Lease (krawl:task:lock:<job>)
nodes.rationale: Lease expires rather than released, since jittered schedules would otherwise let every pod run it; length is 2x jitter clamped below period.

nodes.label: TLSH fuzzy-hash similarity
nodes.rationale: Events (attack bodies + files) shown when TLSH distance <= threshold; diff 0 = identical.

nodes.label: HTMX Fragment Pagination Pattern
nodes.rationale: Each table is a server-rendered HTMX fragment that swaps itself (hx-target closest .htmx-container) with Prev/Next links carrying every filter and sort in the query string; threat_pager centralizes this by taking a URL with filters but no page/page_size and appending them.

nodes.label: Database Schema (AccessLog, AttackDetection, IpStats, CredentialAttempt, CategoryHistory)
nodes.norm_label: database schema (accesslog, attackdetection, ipstats, credentialattempt, categoryhistory)

nodes.label: IP Categorization Model
nodes.rationale: Scores IPs on method distribution, robots.txt violations, timing anomalies, UA diversity, attack URLs.

nodes.label: Krawl Architecture
nodes.rationale: Cloud-native deception honeypot built on FastAPI; wastes attacker resources with infinite spider-trap pages.

nodes.label: Database Migrations (runner.py)
nodes.rationale: Only ALTER-level changes (columns, indexes) that create_all() cannot apply; idempotent and dialect-agnostic so nothing is run by hand.

nodes.label: Frontend Architecture (Jinja2 SSR + Alpine.js + HTMX + Leaflet + Chart.js)
nodes.norm_label: frontend architecture (jinja2 ssr + alpine.js + htmx + leaflet + chart.js)
nodes.rationale: Alpine handles tab state/modals, HTMX handles pagination and fragments, so tables are server-rendered partials.

nodes.label: OOP + Strong Typing (dataclasses, TypedDict, Enums)
nodes.rationale: Prefers explicit, typed, future-proof code over compact one-liners.

nodes.label: Hidden Real Services on Secret Paths (Vaultwarden, Grafana, Nextcloud)
nodes.norm_label: hidden real services on secret paths (vaultwarden, grafana, nextcloud)

nodes.norm_label: request assets table (urls from raw requests)

nodes.rationale: Sort, order and page size ride on .threat-table data attributes so the panel search box and 2+ IPs toggle can reload without dropping sort or page size.

nodes.label: OpenRouter Provider
nodes.rationale: Recommended for cost-effective generation; free models are rate limited per day.

nodes.label: Self-Hosted LLM (llama.cpp / Ollama)
nodes.rationale: Maximum privacy and zero cost; OpenAI-compatible API via openai_base_url. Ollama trades small overhead for easier model management vs raw llama.cpp.

nodes.label: AI-Generated Deception Pages
nodes.rationale: Attackers' requests drive generation, so attackers help build the fake vulnerable attack surface; pages are cached in DB so each path costs at most one API call.

nodes.label: AI Page Generation Flow (cache -> enabled -> daily limit -> generate -> cache)
nodes.norm_label: ai page generation flow (cache -> enabled -> daily limit -> generate -> cache)
nodes.rationale: Cached pages are always served regardless of AI status; fallback to standard honeypot on disabled/limit keeps behavior safe.

nodes.label: AI Daily Request Limit (max_daily_requests)
nodes.rationale: Prevents unexpected API costs; cached pages keep being served when limit is reached.

nodes.label: SQL Injection and XSS Detection
nodes.rationale: Randomized DB errors per request increase SQLMap noise.

nodes.label: wordlists.json Customization
nodes.rationale: Loaded once at startup; falls back to built-in defaults if missing/invalid.

nodes.label: Credential Capture Decoy Forms
nodes.rationale: Login forms POST to honeypot paths (/admin/login, /wp-login.php, /phpmyadmin/index.php) which return a generic error, capturing submitted credentials.

nodes.label: Honeypot Deception Pages
nodes.rationale: Templates mimic real admin/WordPress/phpMyAdmin pages so crawlers and attackers interact and reveal intent.

nodes.label: IP Categories (attacker, bad_crawler, good_crawler, regular_user, unknown)
nodes.norm_label: ip categories (attacker, bad_crawler, good_crawler, regular_user, unknown)

nodes.label: IP Origins Map (Leaflet, clustered)
nodes.rationale: Basemap desaturated so category colours are the only saturated element.

nodes.label: Map Tile Provider Config
nodes.rationale: Esri dark canvas default needs no key; raster templates only since map is Leaflet; API key is public by necessity.

nodes.label: Threats Tab (TLSH campaigns)
nodes.rationale: Fuzzy hashing groups webshell variants into one campaign rather than unrelated one-off hits.

nodes.label: Dashboard Design System Tokens
nodes.rationale: Tokens defined once in dashboard.css; honey colour reserved for honeypot triggers; log data is mono; JS reads category colors via krawlCategoryColors().

nodes.label: Attachment Extraction from Raw Requests
nodes.rationale: Reconstructed from stored raw request; bodies >64KB never buffered; treat downloads as hostile.

nodes.label: Prometheus Metrics Endpoint (/<secret>/metrics)
nodes.rationale: Lives under secret path so it is not publicly discoverable.

nodes.label: Secret Prefix-Based Routing
nodes.rationale: Dashboard/API/HTMX routers mounted under /{secret}, so honeypot catch-all only matches non-secret paths; removes need for _is_dashboard_path checks.

nodes.label: Unprefixed /api Requests Served as Honeypot
nodes.rationale: Calls without the secret path are indistinguishable from scans and intentionally receive honeypot pages.

nodes.label: Grafana Dashboard (generated by build_grafana_dashboard.py)
nodes.rationale: Generated from script so root and Helm copies stay in step; edit script not JSON.

nodes.label: Write Buffer Metrics (per-pod)
nodes.rationale: Process-local buffer so graphed per pod and dropped rows summed.

nodes.label: Aggregate Metrics with max() not sum()
nodes.norm_label: aggregate metrics with max() not sum()
nodes.rationale: Counters shared in Redis so every pod reports cluster totals; summing multiplies by replica count.

nodes.label: Client IP Proxy Header Priority (CF-Connecting-IP, X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP)
nodes.norm_label: client ip proxy header priority (cf-connecting-ip, x-forwarded-for, x-real-ip)

nodes.label: Cloudflare Banlist Sync
nodes.rationale: Behind Cloudflare, origin bans block CF edges not attackers; banning at the edge via Account IP List + WAF rule uses the real client IP Cloudflare observed.

nodes.label: Deploying Behind a Reverse Proxy or CDN
nodes.norm_label: deploying behind a reverse proxy or cdn

nodes.label: Automatic Cloudflare WAF Rule (ip.src in $krawl_banlist)
nodes.rationale: Created once at save and idempotent; sync only updates the list to avoid ruleset churn.

nodes.label: Full List Replacement Sync (PUT)
nodes.rationale: Full replace rather than incremental updates keeps sync simple.

nodes.label: Wildcard Subdomain Deception
nodes.rationale: Every guessed subdomain resolves to Krawl, giving visibility into attack surface mapping; wildcard cert avoids CT-log leakage.

nodes.label: Deployment Modes (scalable vs standalone)
nodes.rationale: scalable uses PostgreSQL+Redis with RollingUpdate and multiple replicas; standalone uses SQLite+in-memory cache, single replica, Recreate strategy because state cannot be shared

nodes.label: Existing Secret Pattern (External Secrets / Vault)
nodes.rationale: Credentials (dashboard, AI, canary, CloudFlare, postgres, redis, map) can come from externally managed Secrets; setting name skips chart-managed Secret and keeps sensitive values out of ConfigMap

nodes.label: PostgreSQL Tuning (shared_buffers, work_mem, shmSize)
nodes.rationale: Server defaults too small for busy sensors; random_page_cost/effective_io_concurrency left at rotational defaults since SSD values harm network volumes; /dev/shm raised to 256Mi because parallel VACUUM exhausts the 64Mi k8s default; memory limit kept above shared_buffers since OOM kills wipe autovacuum stats

nodes.label: Real Client IP Preservation (externalTrafficPolicy Local / Traefik trustedIPs)
nodes.norm_label: real client ip preservation (externaltrafficpolicy local / traefik trustedips)
nodes.rationale: Krawl must see the actual attacker IP rather than the proxy IP, so Service uses externalTrafficPolicy Local and Traefik must trust forwarded headers

nodes.label: Uvicorn Runtime Bounds (limitConcurrency, backlog, graceful shutdown)
nodes.norm_label: uvicorn runtime bounds (limitconcurrency, backlog, graceful shutdown)
nodes.rationale: One worker per pod; scale replicaCount instead of multiple schedulers per pod; worker recycling disabled by default because it loses warm caches

nodes.label: Standalone replicaCount=1 guard
nodes.rationale: fail render if standalone and replicaCount>1 because SQLite and in-memory state cannot be shared

nodes.label: Startup probe on /<secret_path>/healthz or TCP fallback
nodes.norm_label: startup probe on /<secret_path>/healthz or tcp fallback
nodes.rationale: secret_path auto-generated at runtime is unknowable at template time, so probe falls back to TCP to avoid hitting the honeypot catch-all

nodes.label: Sorted -c config args
nodes.rationale: keys sorted so helm upgrade does not diff on Go map ordering

nodes.label: Metrics endpoint /<secret_path>/metrics
nodes.rationale: ServiceMonitor only rendered when metrics enabled and secret_path fixed, since an auto-generated path cannot be scraped

nodes.label: Redis maxmemory volatile-lru policy
nodes.rationale: volatile-lru evicts only TTL'd krawl:cache:* keys and never krawl:counter:* metrics; maxmemory ~75% of limit to leave fragmentation headroom

nodes.label: rolloutOnUpgrade (release-revision pod annotation)
nodes.rationale: Every helm upgrade restarts pods so reused image tags are re-pulled, since imagePullPolicy only applies at pod start

nodes.label: Service sessionAffinity None
nodes.rationale: Scalable mode keeps sessions/cache in Redis, so stickiness only creates uneven hot pods

nodes.label: brand Template Global
nodes.rationale: Set once at startup via build_brand from dashboard.branding config; no link configured renders a span instead of a dead anchor.

nodes.label: window.__MAP_TILES__ Server-Side Tile Config
nodes.rationale: Tile key is necessarily public since the browser fetches tiles directly, so it should be restricted by domain at the provider.

nodes.label: Tarpit
nodes.rationale: Opt-in; makes crawling expensive for LLM training scrapers; async wait costs a connection not a worker.

nodes.label: Global Canary Page Counter (token_tries)
nodes.rationale: Global (not per-IP) counter injects canary link every Nth honeypot page so link-following crawlers eventually trigger an alert.

nodes.label: Tarpit Delay (delay_seconds)
nodes.rationale: 1-5s is cheap drag; >30s clients time out which ends the tarpit early.

nodes.label: CDN Range Exclusion (exclude_cdn)
nodes.rationale: Behind a CDN the recorded IP may be an edge node; blocking it takes the CDN offline. Ranges fetched live and cached 1h.

nodes.label: FORMATS Registry + format_banlist(fwtype, ips)
nodes.rationale: Each format is a function registered by name; adding a key immediately exposes a new fwtype.

nodes.label: Server Public IP Discovery (ipify, ident.me, ifconfig.me)
nodes.norm_label: server public ip discovery (ipify, ident.me, ifconfig.me)
nodes.rationale: Discovered once at startup to exclude the server's own IP from statistics; services tried in sequence as fallback.

nodes.label: External APIs
nodes.rationale: All external calls run in background tasks so they never block incoming requests.

nodes.label: IP Category Taxonomy (attacker, bad_crawler, good_crawler, regular_user, unknown)
nodes.norm_label: ip category taxonomy (attacker, bad_crawler, good_crawler, regular_user, unknown)

nodes.label: Ban Override (force ban/unban/reset)
nodes.rationale: Manual override of automatic ban decisions; changes take effect on next banlist export cycle (every 5 minutes).

nodes.label: Campaign Cluster (TLSH-grouped payloads)
nodes.rationale: Target path leads in the UI because humans recognise it; TLSH digest identifies the campaign to the DB so it stays in the tooltip. State rides on data-* attributes so search reloads keep sort/filter/page size.

nodes.label: CDN Range Exclusion on Export
nodes.rationale: Drops IPs inside published CDN provider ranges (Cloudflare, Fastly, CloudFront, Google, Bunny) fetched at export time.

nodes.label: Firewall Export Formats (raw, iptables, nftables)
nodes.rationale: Direct URL lets OPNsense and external systems fetch the list directly.

nodes.label: HTMX Fragment Pagination Pattern
nodes.rationale: Prev/Next buttons hx-get the same endpoint with page +/-1 and swap innerHTML of the closest .htmx-container.

nodes.label: Recurring Campaign Artifact (shared filename across IPs)
nodes.norm_label: recurring campaign artifact (shared filename across ips)
nodes.rationale: Same filename from many IPs signals a recurring campaign artifact such as a webshell or script upload name.

nodes.label: Referer Bait Tracking
nodes.rationale: Shows which referring URL (bait) led the attacker onto which trap path.

nodes.label: Configuration tab as config.yaml echo
nodes.rationale: Read-only config tab mirrors config.yaml section names and keys in mono so operators can map what they see to the file they edit; sensitive values masked, full key/value in title because lines are truncated.

nodes.label: Scheduled task display (TasksMaster)
nodes.rationale: Disabled tasks show 'on demand only' rather than TasksMaster's default cron, which would claim a schedule the task doesn't have; a pod chip indicates single-pod ownership vs runs on every pod; only the purge task takes options rendered as checkboxes.
